S9.01.needs: a workspace folder open in VS Code
S9.01.note: The @ picker lists files, folders and symbols; projects, models and skills are not listed in this picker in the code.
steps: Sign in, open the AGI Code sidebar and click the "Describe a task…" box.
Type @ followed by part of a file name, for example @app.
Look for a list labelled "Workspace files and symbols" under the box, and check that it narrows as you type more letters.
Clear the text and type a different query; the list should change to match.
Note: the code searches workspace files, folders and symbols. It did not show projects, models or skills in this picker.
S9.01.where: AGI Code sidebar > click the "Describe a task…" box > type @ and a few letters of a file or symbol name

S9.02.note: If no model is listed the popover shows "No models available".
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and find the model button under the chat box; it shows "Auto" at first.
Click it to open the "Select model" list grouped by model family.
Pick a different model.
Check that the button now shows the model you picked and that the next reply uses it.
Alternative: open the Command Palette and run "Code: Select Model", then pick a model.
S9.02.where: AGI Code sidebar > model button under the chat box (title "Model", shows "Auto" by default) > pick a model in the "Select model" list

S9.06.needs: a cloud account with at least one project
S9.06.note: The last step (the chat actually runs in the project) was not traced in the code.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Projects".
Pick one of your projects from the list.
In the project detail list, choose "Use in this chat".
Open the same project again and check that its row now says "Used in this chat" with a check mark.
Send a message in the chat and check that the project is applied to it.
S9.06.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Projects" > pick a project > "Use in this chat"

labels.text: Select a workspace folder for this operation

S9.07.needs: two folders open in one VS Code window
S9.07.note: The code shows a folder list only. No field for typing a repository URL or path was found for this choice. The exact command that opens this list was not identified.
steps: Open two folders in one VS Code window (File > Open Folder twice, or add a folder to the workspace).
Close every editor tab so no file is active.
Run an AGI Code command that works on a folder.
Look for the list titled "Select a workspace folder for this operation" and pick a folder; the folder path is shown beside each name.
Check that the command runs in the folder you picked.
S9.07.where: Two or more folders open in one VS Code window with no file open > an AGI Code action that needs a folder > list "Select a workspace folder for this operation"

S9.10.needs: a task that asks for approval (shell commands ask first in the mode described in the Mode list)
S9.10.note: The card's buttons are built from the words Approve and Deny in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts, so the exact button text may read "Approve once" or "Approve for session".
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and send a task that runs a shell command, such as listing files.
When the "Approval needed" card appears, read the action it names.
Compare the choices offered (once, for session, deny) and note what each one covers.
Choose one and check that the run continues or stops as chosen.
Open the Command Palette, run "Code: Permissions" and check the "Add a rule" entry, which lets you pick allow, ask first or block for a site, tool or command.
S9.10.where: AGI Code sidebar > chat asks to run a shell command (approval card "Approval needed") > choose Approve or Deny; or Command Palette > "Code: Permissions" > "Add a rule"

S9.19.needs: a sign-in or setup that lets AGI run tools
S9.19.note: The time is shown only when the run reports it.
steps: Send a task that makes AGI read or change files so tools run.
Find the "Activity" summary under the reply, which shows a count such as "3 actions".
Click it to open the list of steps.
Check that the steps are in the order they ran, each with its state (running, done or error).
Check that finished steps show a time such as "· 1.2s" after their name.
S9.19.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a task that uses tools > "Activity" summary under the reply > click it to open the list of tool steps

S9.21.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with at least one cloud task
S9.21.note: The code shows a grouped list with headings, not a board with a column per status.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Look at the list titled with "Cloud tasks"; tasks are grouped under the headings "Needs you", "Working", "Ready for review", "Done" and "Stopped".
Compare the groups with the task states shown in each row.
Start or wait for a cloud task in another state and check that it moves to the matching group.

S9.22.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode/src for "Step N of", "Step " with a value, "stepper", "step-dot", "steps-indicator" and "wizard". No step indicator or stepper was found; the only related item is onboarding inline actions in the sidebar CSS.

S9.24.note: The code opens results beside the current editor (showLlmResultInNewTab in apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/applyEdit.ts), but no app control to resize that split was found; the resize is VS Code's own editor divider. Not confirmed that the pane pairing matches Expected.

S9.25.note: Searched apps/extension-vscode for docking, left, right, bottom, floating and layout code. The app registers one sidebar view (apps/extension-vscode/package.json, views agi-workforce.sidebar); moving it is done by VS Code, and no layout-saving code was found.

S9.27.needs: a file open in the editor and a reply with a code block
S9.27.note: Only the "Apply" path was traced to the diff provider; other ways of proposing a change were not checked.
steps: Open a file in the editor and ask AGI in the sidebar to change it, so a reply includes a code block.
Click the "Apply" button on that code block.
Wait for the change to appear in the open file, with removed lines shaded red and added lines marked "+" in the gutter.
Read the line above the change, which starts with "Changes:" and names the file.
Compare with Expected: the lines are readable before you click "Accept" or "Reject".
S9.27.where: AGI Code sidebar > a reply with a code block > "Apply" button on the block > the editor shows the proposed change with "Accept" and "Reject" links above it

S9.29.needs: a paid AGI Cloud plan (Free accounts do not get this meter in the code path checked)
S9.29.note: The position of the usage bar in the sidebar was not confirmed; the bar is only shown when the account has usage data.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Account & Usage".
Find the "Cloud quota" section and the row that starts "Cloud usage:" with the percent used and "Plan:" beside it.
Open the AGI Code sidebar and find the usage bar labelled "AGI Managed Cloud plan usage" (with "Usage" to show details if it is collapsed).
Check the percent, the reset text in the bar (or "No reset pending") and that the bar matches the palette row.
Optional: with VoiceOver on, focus the bar and check that it reads the percent.
S9.29.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > "Cloud usage: N% used" row; the sidebar usage bar is labelled "AGI Managed Cloud plan usage"

labels.text: Buy credits in Settings > Billing on Web

S9.30.needs: a paid account that has a credit balance
S9.30.note: The palette row does not show the balance itself; the balance is in the sidebar usage list, which needs the usage bar to be expanded.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Account & Usage".
Look for the row "Add credits" with the description "Buy credits in Settings > Billing on Web".
Check the sidebar usage list titled "Managed Cloud usage limits" for the credit row with its balance and an "Add credits" button.
Choose "Add credits" and check that the web billing page opens.
Compare the balance shown with Expected: the balance and the add-credits action sit together.
S9.30.where: Command Palette > "Code: Account & Usage" > "Add credits" (shown only when the account has a credit balance)

S9.31.note: Trusted folders appear only when the CLI offers trust settings; "Turned off" tools appear only when some are off.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Permissions".
Read the list: "This session" shows the mode and tools; "Rules for every session" lists saved rules; "Trusted folders" lists trusted folders.
Compare the list with what the assistant may do: check the mode label and any "Turned off" tools.
Pick "Add a rule" and look at the choices offered (allow, ask first, block) without saving, then cancel.

S9.32.needs: a task that triggers an approval (a shell command)
S9.32.note: The approve button text is built from "Approve" in packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts, so the exact wording may be "Approve once" or "Approve for session".
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and send a task that asks AGI to run a shell command.
When the "Approval needed" card appears, read the action named in the card.
Click one of the approve buttons (once or for the session) and check that the card shows an approved state and the run continues.
Send another such task, click "Deny" (or type guidance in the box and press Enter) and check that the run stops or changes course.
"Abort turn" stops the whole reply; check that it ends the run.
S9.32.where: AGI Code sidebar > send a task that needs an action approved > "Approval needed" card with Approve and Deny buttons

S9.35.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with a running cloud task
S9.35.note: The list refreshes every 15 seconds in the code; the steps-done text and latest action were not traced to a visible line in the detail view.
steps: Open the Command Palette and run "Code: Show Cloud Tasks".
Under the "Working" group, pick a task that is running.
Read its state and description, and open its detail with the task's title.
Wait about 15 seconds and check that the state or progress has changed when it has changed in the cloud.
S9.35.where: Command Palette > "Code: Show Cloud Tasks" > group "Working" > pick a running task

S9.38.note: No keyboard shortcut that opens this list was found in package.json. Typing / in the chat box opens a menu without the filter box. Cmd or Ctrl+Shift+P opens VS Code's own palette, not this one.
steps: Open the AGI Code sidebar and click the "/" button beside the chat box.
Check that the list opens with a "Filter actions…" box focused.
Type part of a command name, for example "model", and check that the list narrows.
Press Enter on the highlighted item and check that it runs.
S9.38.where: AGI Code sidebar > click the "/" button (title "Commands") > type in the "Filter actions…" box > press Enter on a choice
